calls.head: Iron sharpens iron
calls.body: The Capitals are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Kings are the best at preventing dangerous shots. Hot take: the Capitals break through anyway.

calls.head: A shadow job for Protas, Jenner and Wilson
calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Jenner and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Kings’ first line is Panarin, Byfield and Kempe.
calls.call: The Capitals’ L2 (Protas, Jenner and Wilson) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ first line, against about 30% with no line matching.

surprises.head: Darcy Kuemper stole one
surprises.body: Kuemper allowed 2 goals on 32 shots, worth 5.0 expected goals: 3.0 fewer than expected. That is more than Los Angeles’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 70 starts.

surprises.head: Washington found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Los Angeles is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: Washington’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 7.0% (about 6.5% against Los Angeles) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: At last, a first win for the Kings
paras: The Kings won for the first time this season, at the seventh try, after starting 0-4-2. It was a busy first period. The Kings’ Quinton Byfield left in the first period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Ryan Leonard got the scoring started for the Capitals midway through the period. Cole Hutson made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period, but they didn’t score again. Adrian Kempe and Artemi Panarin scored 31 seconds apart later in the period to tie it 2-2. Erik Gustafsson scored his first goal for Los Angeles on the power play early in the third to put the Kings ahead and complete the comeback. Kempe scored his second of the night just over four minutes later to make it 4-2. Scott Laughton added an empty-net goal with less than two minutes left to make it 5-2. Panarin finished with a goal and two assists.

The score flatters the Kings: the Capitals had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Caps win about seven in ten. Darcy Kuemper was the difference, stopping 30 of 32. Logan Thompson stopped 21 of 25 for the Capitals. The Kings improved to 1-4-2 and climbed out of last place in the NHL, while the Capitals fell to 5-4-0, slipping to fourth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Kings were the last team in the NHL without a win.
The Capitals’ Matt Roy was back in the lineup after missing six games.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
